title: Evaluation of the efficacy of corticosteroids in septic arthritis in adults: Randomized double-blind controlled trial [CORSAR]
official: Evaluation of the efficacy of corticosteroids in septic arthritis in adults: Randomized double-blind controlled trial [CORSAR]
summary: Main objective: To evaluate whether corticosteroid administration alongside antibiotic therapy modifies joint prognosis in adult septic arthritis at 24 weeks
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Documented septic arthritis (microorganism identified intra-articularly by culture or PCR, or by turbid synovial fluid with positive Gram stain, or positive blood cultures) - Effective antibiotic therapy initiated within ≤ 3 days
3. Effective antibiotic therapy initiated within ≤ 3 days
4. Signed informed consent
5. Affiliation to a health insurance system
6. Ability to read, write, and understand French
Exclusion criteria:
1. Polyarticular septic arthritis (≥ 2 joints)
2. Current pregnancy
3. Breastfeeding women
4. Septic arthritis of small joints (e.g., fingers: PIP, DIP, MCP; toes: MTP, or pubic symphysis, or sternoclavicular joint)
5. Patients under legal protection (e.g., guardianship)
6. Participation in another interventional drug clinical trial
7. Patient unable to provide informed consent
8. Systemic sclerosis
9. Pyomyositis
10. Diabetic foot infection
11. Current corticosteroid therapy for another indication
12. Presence of prosthetic joint or osteosynthesis material in the affected joint
13. Inability to take oral medication
14. Contraindication to corticosteroids (notably decompensated diabetes or uncontrolled psychiatric disorders)
15. Associated endocarditis
16. Active hyperthyroidism
17. Septic shock
18. Severe soft tissue wound overlying the affected joint
19. Aplastic chemotherapy
20. Neutropenia (defined as neutrophils < 500/mm³)
21. Mycobacterial infection
22. Fungal infection
23. Sickle cell disease
